blind_spots_patched: Original Chapters 1-6 omitted consolidated goodwill concentration (Key Audit Matter with recurring FY25 impairments), doubling of unrecognized deferred tax assets on subsidiary losses, ongoing multi-state US generic drug price-fixing antitrust litigation through 2028, and the FY26 Rs 1,100 Cr buyback approved amid contracting operating cash flow.

Original Chapters 4-5 vaguely noted rival PPAR agonists in US PBC without quantifying the clinical efficacy and two-year launch head start of Gilead's Livdelzi and Ipsen's Iqirvo, and omitted that Zydus's Mirabegron settlement window through September 2027 is shared with Lupin and MSN.

Original Chapters 4-5 treated USFDA cGMP compliance risk as confined to Indian plants (Moraiya and Baddi), omitting the mid-November 2026 USFDA inspection and 4 Form 483 observations at UK subsidiary LiqMeds as well as the November 25, 2026 EIR clearances for SEZ II Ahmedabad and Ankleshwar API Unit-2.
assumptions_changed: WEAKENED: USFDA cGMP compliance risk is concentrated at Baddi (June 2026 Warning Letter) and Moraiya (5 Form 483 observations in October 2026, EIR pending).

CONFIRMED: International Markets (11% of FY26 mix, +33% YoY to >Rs 10 bn in Q2 FY27) is scaling via differentiated branded generics and partnerships including the 2026 Sri Lanka JV with Sunshine Healthcare Lanka.

CONFIRMED: Despite gross debt rising to Rs 13,966 Cr (Sep 2026, 0.62x Net Debt/EBITDA) and FY26 CFO dropping to Rs 2,117 Cr (44% CFO/EBITDA), Zydus maintains a healthy balance sheet and liquidity cushion.
